proposed_core_edits.reason: The cited node is not a safe logical premise in its present form.  The literal class in JMS Theorem 3.2 requires bounded \(Y\) while its Gaussian treatment residual has conditionally full support.  Under \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\), bounded \(Y\) implies bounded \(E[Y\mid X,T]=\theta T+f(X)\); conditional full support of \(T\) therefore forces \(\theta=0\).  Moreover, Appendix D equation (56) supplies only the fuzzy nuisance-product/log term, whereas equations (57)--(58) obtain the separate root-\(N\) term from a Gaussian-outcome witness outside the literal bounded-outcome class.  Thus the source does not validate the node's claim that one source experiment, or one fuzzy construction, delivers the displayed sum.  The node has no live inbound dependency, while the valid nuisance-product content is already retained in \(\textup{lem:jms-support-localized-product-benchmark}\); deletion is therefore coherent and requires no replacement edge.

proposed.comparator_claim: The displayed rate in Theorem 3.2 contains nuisance-product and parametric terms, but its literal bounded-outcome class is incompatible with a nonzero partially linear slope under conditionally full-support Gaussian treatment noise and \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\). Appendix D equation (56) supplies the nuisance-product/log conclusion on the localized fuzzy supports, whereas equations (57)--(58) use an unbounded Gaussian-outcome witness for the separate parametric term. Theorem 5.4 gives a fixed-positive-cumulant ACE point-estimation upper bound on a separate class.
proposed.matched_by: The conditionally transferred support-localized Gaussian product lower bound, the separately proved compatible parametric path, and Open-ended Questions 7--9

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 characterize expected-length adaptation over unions in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
The paper obtains composite-hypothesis lower bounds by moment-matched priors and chi-square control of normal mixtures.
Theorem 5 rules out second-order PLM orthogonality under Gaussian residuals, while Theorems 8--10 construct higher-order moments under non-Gaussian residuals.
Theorem 2 establishes coverage and interval-length control for the filtered union, while Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient.

prose_updates.tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). On supplied-fit sequences satisfying the stated conditional-transfer compatibility, the certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\): the nuisance-product/log term comes from the transferred support-localized JMS fuzzy construction, while \(n^{-1/2}\) comes from a separate compatible two-point family proved inside the present class. The literal full-class statement of JMS Theorem 3.2 is not used for this sum because its bounded-\(Y\), full-support Gaussian-treatment conditions force slope degeneracy under conditional outcome orthogonality, and its displayed root-\(N\) witness has unbounded Gaussian outcome. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is confined to the lower subexperiment. The within-non-Gaussian or constrained-risk branchwise converse and removal of the Gaussian logarithm remain open; no matching Pareto frontier or global union-supremum improvement is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Published structure-agnostic PLM theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length. The literal bounded-outcome formulation of JMS Theorem 3.2 also cannot be transferred wholesale to the present Gaussian branch: with conditionally full-support Gaussian treatment and \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\), bounded \(Y\) forces the partially linear slope to vanish, while its Appendix D root-\(N\) witness uses an unbounded Gaussian outcome.
project_justification.niche: The informative object is the two-coordinate expected-length region; the global union supremum remains governed by the Gaussian coordinate.
project_justification.fill: The proved upper component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion. The Gaussian converse is certified at \(d_n^-\) only under explicit conditional transfer of the source-localized nuisance-product supports and a compatible nonempty two-point path. The localized fuzzy construction supplies the product/log term, and the paper's own two-point argument supplies the parametric term; their maximum is converted to the displayed sum. The unsafe aggregate JMS lemma is removed rather than used as a full-class inclusion theorem. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is auxiliary to that lower subexperiment. The selector impossibility theorem closes the bounded-chi-square cross-branch fuzzy route at strong separation, while the actual strong-regime lower frontier remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis inform two distinct pieces of the Gaussian-coordinate argument, but their literal full-class Theorem 3.2 is not used as a logical premise here. Its statement combines bounded \(Y\), conditionally full-support Gaussian treatment noise, and \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\); those conditions force a nonzero partially linear slope to be impossible because \(E[Y\mid X,T]=\theta T+f(X)\) would otherwise be unbounded in \(T\). Consistently with this mismatch, Appendix D equation (56) derives only the nuisance-product/log term at the retained \(\Lambda_n\) factor from moment-matched fuzzy supports, whereas equations (57)--(58) derive the parametric term using an unbounded Gaussian-outcome model. The present theorem conditionally transfers only the support-localized equation-(56) construction and independently proves the root-\(n\) term on a compatible embedded two-point path; it combines the two lower bounds through \(\max\{x,y\}\ge (x+y)/2\). Their Theorem 5.4 informs the fixed-separation ACE component but does not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. The auxiliary condition \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) is not attributed to their envelope and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length lower subexperiment. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned PLM residual. Cai and Low's 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier together with the conditional Gaussian coordinate just described; it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), not \(d_n\), and is conditional on two explicit compatibility requirements: transfer of the support-localized JMS fuzzy priors after outcome rescaling, and existence of a nonempty Gaussian two-point path around a compatible anchor. The cited localized fuzzy support supplies only the nuisance-product/log term; the parametric term is proved separately inside the paper and the two bounds are combined only afterward. The literal bounded-\(Y\) statement of JMS Theorem 3.2 cannot provide a direct full-class inclusion, because full-support Gaussian treatment plus conditional outcome orthogonality makes that bounded-outcome class slope-degenerate, and its Appendix D parametric witness instead has unbounded Gaussian outcome. The auxiliary subclass \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) is used only for this converse. The upper theorem needs none of these lower-experiment restrictions and does not identify a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early bounded-chi-square cross-branch Rademacher/Hermite route is resolved negatively at strong separation because the common-fit selector makes the mixtures asymptotically singular; a within-non-Gaussian or constrained-risk experiment is still required for the actual lower frontier.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All upper-frontier inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the upper theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The Gaussian lower theorem is explicitly conditional: for positive nuisance-product indices, only the source-localized fuzzy supports are invoked, with treatment radius \(\varepsilon_{g,n}/K\), outcome fit \(\widehat q/A\), and outcome radius \(\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\), followed by the pushforward \(S_A(x,t,y)=(x,t,Ay)\). A separate compatible two-point path supplies \(n^{-1/2}\). No direct inclusion of the literal JMS Theorem 3.2 class is asserted, because its bounded-outcome condition excludes the unbounded Gaussian-outcome root-\(N\) witness and is slope-degenerate under the present orthogonality condition. The novel restriction \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) defines only \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and is used only in that converse. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The branchwise converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(N=3n\).  By \(\textup{def:projected-experiment}\), concatenating the mutually independent folds \(D_K,D_D,D_A\) identifies \(Q_P\) with \(P^{\otimes N}\).  Thus every interval measurable with respect to the three folds is an interval in the \(N\)-observation experiment.

We first establish the nuisance-product lower bound on an index for which \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\).  Define
\[
 a_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}}{K},
 \qquad
 b_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{q,n}}{KA}.
\]
The constants \(A\) and \(K\) in \(\mathrm{CT2}\) do not depend on \(n\), so the product-smallness hypothesis in the theorem gives
\[
 a_Nb_N
 =\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K^2A}
 =o\!\left((\log N)^{-1/2}\right).
\]
Condition \(\mathrm{CT2}\) therefore permits application of \(\textup{lem:jms-support-localized-product-benchmark}\), with \(s=8\), source supplied fit \((\widehat g,\widehat q/A)\), and source radii \((a_N,b_N)\).  This invocation supplies only the nuisance-product/logarithmic mechanism from the two moment-matched fuzzy supports; no parametric term is attributed to that construction.

Let \(\widehat\theta\) be any real-valued estimator in the transformed \(N\)-observation experiment.  For source observations \(z_1,\ldots,z_N\), define
\[
 \widehat\vartheta_R(z_1,\ldots,z_N)
 =A^{-1}\widehat\theta(S_Az_1,\ldots,S_Az_N),
 \qquad S_A(x,t,y)=(x,t,Ay).
\]
Take \(\gamma=3/4\); since \(\alpha<1/2\), one has \(\gamma>\alpha\).  The cited support-localized benchmark yields \(i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(R\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_{i,N})\) such that
\[
 R^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
 \left|\widehat\vartheta_R-\vartheta(R)\right|
 \ge c_\gamma a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \right\}\ge\gamma .
\]
Set \(P=R\circ S_A^{-1}\).  By \(\mathrm{CT2}\), this law satisfies
\[
 P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n},
 \qquad
 (\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P),
 \qquad
 \theta_0(P)=A\vartheta(R).
\]
Because \(S_A\) is a measurable bijection and \(Q_P=P^{\otimes N}\), the preceding probability is exactly
\[
 Q_P\!\left\{
 \left|\widehat\theta-\theta_0(P)\right|
 \ge c_\gamma A a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \right\}\ge\gamma .
\]
The use of the source radius \(b_N=\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\) before the pushforward is essential, and it gives
\[
 A a_Nb_N
 =\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K^2}.
\]

Let \(\ell_n=1\vee\log(1/\varepsilon_{g,n})\).  On the present positive-product index, \(0<\varepsilon_{g,n}\le C_{\mathrm{env}}\).  Since \(K\ge e(1\vee C_{\mathrm{env}})\),
\[
 \log(1/a_N)=\log(K/\varepsilon_{g,n})\ge\ell_n.
\]
There is a universal constant \(c_0\ge1\) such that \(\log(3n)\le c_0\log(en)\) for every \(n\ge1\).  Consequently, using \(\textup{def:rate-scales}\),
\[
 A a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \ge c_1\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 \min\!\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{\ell_n}{\log(en)}\right)^3\right\}
 =c_1\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n,
\]
where \(c_1>0\) is independent of \(n\).  Hence every estimator has error at least \(c_2\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\), with probability at least \(\gamma\), at some law in the transferred fuzzy support.

By \(\mathrm{CT2}\), every law in that support belongs to \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\), is compatible with the supplied pair, and hence belongs to \(\mathcal U_n\) by \(\textup{def:gaussian-nondegenerate-subclass}\) and \(\textup{def:honesty-union}\).  The assumed union honesty of \(C_n\) therefore implies honesty over this transferred support.  Apply \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) with \(r=c_2\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\), \(\beta=\gamma\), and this support as \(\mathscr R\).  Since \(\gamma-\alpha>0\), there is \(c_3>0\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c_3\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n.
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}=0\), the same inequality is automatic because its right-hand side is zero; no fuzzy-support invocation is then needed.

We now obtain the parametric term by a separate compatible two-point experiment.  Set
\[
 \beta=\frac{\alpha+1/2}{2},
 \qquad \alpha<\beta<\frac12.
\]
Use the covariate law \(P_{X,n}\) and functions \(g_{*,n},q_{*,n}\) furnished by \(\mathrm{CT1}\).  For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), put
\[
 v_0=0,
 \qquad
 v_1=\Delta=\frac{h}{\sqrt N},
 \qquad
 P_j=P_{n,v_j},
\]
where \(h>0\) will be fixed independently of \(n\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\Delta\le h_0\), so \(\mathrm{CT1}\) gives
\[
 P_j\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n},
 \qquad
 (\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P_j).
\]
Under \(P_j\), the defining equations in \(\mathrm{CT1}\) can be rewritten as
\[
 Y=v_jT+\{q_{*,n}(X)-v_jg_{*,n}(X)\}+A\zeta.
\]
Thus the partially linear coefficient is \(\theta_0(P_j)=v_j\), the structural nuisance is \(f_{0,j}=q_{*,n}-v_jg_{*,n}\), and the outcome disturbance is \(\xi_j=A\zeta\).  In particular, independence of \(\zeta\) from \((X,\eta)\), together with \(T=g_{*,n}(X)+\eta\), gives
\[
 E_{P_j}[\xi_j\mid X,T]=0,
 \qquad
 E_{P_j}[\xi_j^2\mid X,T]=A^2\ge c_\xi.
\]
The remaining membership conditions are already part of \(\mathrm{CT1}\).

Under \(P_0\), conditional division of the two Gaussian outcome densities gives the one-observation likelihood ratio
\[
 L=\frac{dP_1}{dP_0}
 =\exp\!\left\{
 \frac{\Delta\eta\{Y-q_{*,n}(X)\}}{A^2}
 -\frac{\Delta^2\eta^2}{2A^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Under \(P_0\), \(\{Y-q_{*,n}(X)\}/A=\zeta\) is standard Gaussian and independent of \(\eta\).  The standard-normal moment-generating identity therefore yields
\[
 E_{P_0}[L^2\mid X,\eta]
 =\exp(\Delta^2\eta^2/A^2).
\]
Since \(\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), direct Gaussian integration gives
\[
 E_{P_0}[L^2]
 =\left(1-\frac{2\Delta^2}{A^2}\right)^{-1/2}.
\]
Independence of the \(N\) observations now implies
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N}\right)
 =\left(1-\frac{2h^2}{A^2N}\right)^{-N/2}-1.
\]
Choose \(h\le A/2\).  Then \(x=2h^2/(A^2N)\le1/2\), and the elementary inequality \(-\log(1-x)\le2x\), valid for \(0\le x\le1/2\), gives
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N}\right)
 \le \exp(2h^2/A^2)-1.
\]
Reduce \(h>0\), if necessary, so that it also satisfies
\[
 \exp(2h^2/A^2)-1\le4(1-2\beta)^2.
\]
This choice depends only on \(\alpha\), \(A\), and the fixed feasibility radius \(h_0\).  By the definition of total variation and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality,
\[
 \left\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12E_{P_0^{\otimes N}}|L_N-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N})}
 \le1-2\beta,
\]
where \(L_N=dP_1^{\otimes N}/dP_0^{\otimes N}\).

For an arbitrary estimator \(\widehat\theta\), define the disjoint events
\[
 A_j=\{|\widehat\theta-v_j|<\Delta/2\},
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Their disjointness and the defining variational inequality imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_0^{\otimes N}(A_0)+P_1^{\otimes N}(A_1)
 &\le P_0^{\otimes N}(A_0)+P_0^{\otimes N}(A_1)
   +\left\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\\
 &\le1+\left\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
It follows that
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}
 P_j^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta-v_j|\ge\frac{h}{2\sqrt N}
 \right\}
 \ge\frac{1-\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{2}
 \ge\beta.
\]
The two laws lie in the honesty union and are compatible with the supplied fits by \(\mathrm{CT1}\).  Applying \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) with \(\mathscr R=\{P_0,P_1\}\) and \(r=h/(2\sqrt N)\) yields a constant \(c_4>0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c_4N^{-1/2}
 \ge c_5n^{-1/2}.
\]

The same supremum is bounded below by the parametric term and by the nuisance-product/logarithmic term.  Using \(\max\{x,y\}\ge(x+y)/2\) and \(\textup{def:rate-scales}\), we conclude that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c\left\{n^{-1/2}
 +\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\right\}
 =c d_n^-.
\]
Here \(c>0\) depends only on \(\alpha\), \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(c_\xi\), because \(A,K,h_0\) have precisely that dependence in \(\mathrm{CT1}\)--\(\mathrm{CT2}\).  Finally, \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal G_n\) and \(\textup{def:length-vector}\) imply \(L_G(C_n)\ge c d_n^-\).  The argument uses the conditional outcome-variance restriction and \(\mathrm{CT1}\)--\(\mathrm{CT2}\) only to form these Gaussian lower-bound subexperiments; neither condition is asserted for the adaptive upper-frontier theorem.
